cases.question: What does the Faros takeaway page report about production incidents as AI adoption changes?
cases.limits: Quotations are frozen from the takeaway page accessed 24 October 2026. The live page is not a test dependency. The sentence that names a randomized effect is fixture-authored because the page describes a within-organization period comparison and does not use the word randomized. The talk sentence is fixture-authored and is not independent corroboration. The full report file was not captured.

sources.title: AI acceleration whiplash takeaways
sources.note: Public takeaway page. Section heading and body are separate anchors.

anchors.text: For every code change merged, the probability of a production incident has more than tripled.
The incidents-to-PR ratio is up 242.7% as teams move from low to high AI adoption.
This is a ratio, not a probability: a single PR can be linked to multiple incidents, and not every incident traces directly to the most recent merge.
It is a measurement of what AI is actually producing across the full software development lifecycle, tracking metric change between periods of lowest and highest AI adoption within each organization.
The period comparison is observational. It is not a randomized causal effect, and it does not show that AI caused the change.

The AI Engineering Impact Report 2026: The Acceleration Whiplash draws on two years of telemetry data from 22,000 developers and more than 4,000 teams across the Faros platform, tracking metric change between each organization's periods of lowest and highest AI adoption.
The frozen takeaway page does not report a randomized effect.
Monthly incidents are up 57.9%.
